items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Terminology 50:1
items.html: “Bearing” means a place where the vessel is fit to clothe the light and yet does not clothe it, by reason of its own choosing. It is a very subtle matter, and it is said only of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head], where there is no clothing in actuality, as above (see “clothing in potential”). And it would never occur to anyone that the vessels of the Guf [body] are more fit for the clothing of the lights than the vessels of the Rosh, and yet there is no clothing in the Rosh but only in the Guf. The reason is that the reflected light of the Rosh does not bear the discernment of clothing, since it stands in the discernment of from below upward, and this standing is a discernment of opposition to the clothing, so that it does not bear the clothing. Understand this well. (Part 4, Chapter 1, Item 5)
